stressCase: A fixed-tick RSR audio event must cross an explicit target binding while the Provider exposes truthful context, decode, pending-load and source lifecycle state in both browser and embedded Android hosts.
donorAdvantage: Experience Fabric already supplies deterministic offline voice caps and bus/render diagnostics; the target candidate reuses that evidence as a donor boundary while implementing only lifecycle observability and cleanup in the actual Web Audio Provider.
regressionCase: In-flight decode entries are removed on resolve/reject, reset stops active sources, ended sources decrement active voice count, provider errors and resume failures become diagnostics, and the existing explicit binding/spatial receipts remain unchanged.
boundaries: Diagnostics are target-runtime observations, not a new world authority or audio semantics owner.
No max-voice cap, bus policy, streaming policy, latency budget or mixing-quality claim was introduced or verified.
The reported decode latency is a local Chromium/Android Emulator observation, not a cross-device performance curve.
No native audio backend, speaker/headphone routing, physical-device acceptance, release signing, store delivery or human listening acceptance is claimed.
No K400 gate is promoted to PASS.
nextCandidate: Use the new diagnostics to audit an explicit target voice/concurrency and streaming policy only if a canonical owner can be established; otherwise move to the next engine bottleneck. Physical-device listening remains a separate human gate.
